task: STAGE 27B — BABYLON 9 RUNTIME WORKBENCH. Stage 27A Spatial Platform Contract and Audit has been accepted and merged to main as PR #529, squash commit fd64ef8e14b5b026cec2d14949115ab681fb0b7d. That acceptance is the explicit authorization to begin Stage 27B. Do not reopen Stage 27A architecture polishing. Read docs/ROADMAP.md, docs/colonisation-redesign/spatial-platform-product-contract.md, docs/colonisation-redesign/spatial-platform-architecture-decision.md, docs/colonisation-redesign/stage-27a-stage26-inheritance-matrix.md, CLAUDE.md, and the relevant Stage 26 isolated workbench/test patterns before implementation. First make the minimal authority-status edits needed so docs/ROADMAP.md, CLAUDE.md and .claude-session-context.md accurately record 27A as accepted/complete and 27B Babylon 9 Runtime Workbench as the current authorized lane; do not use that transition as an excuse for further architecture redesign. Then implement Stage 27B completely as an ISOLATED runtime workbench with NO production map wiring. The production R3F/Three.js map and its rollback path must remain unchanged and production remains on R3F until the later explicitly authorized Stage 27G bakeoff/cutover. Use a modern Babylon 9-class @babylonjs/core release with modular/tree-shakeable ES-module imports; do not restore the deleted/unreviewed Babylon attempt wholesale and do not use the historical Babylon 6 monolithic plan as executable authority. Enforce the renderer-neutral dependency boundary from the accepted architecture: domain/feature code must not import Babylon, Babylon types must not leak through public SpatialSceneContract/MapRuntime contracts, and there must be one renderer adapter boundary with focused import-boundary tests. Implement the long-lived isolated MapRuntime lifecycle needed for the workbench: backend initialization, load renderer-neutral scene state, revisioned contribution updates, resize/DPR handling, suspend/resume or equivalent idle handling, resource rebuild from retained CPU contracts, and explicit disposal of observers/resources/event bridges. Backend selection must attempt WebGPU only after capability/initialization checks and fall back to WebGL2 BEFORE scene/GPU resource creation; backend failure/loss must rebuild from renderer-neutral CPU state rather than preserve hidden backend-specific domain state. Preserve canonical Elite Cartesian coordinates in actual light-years on the CPU. Evaluate Babylon 9 Large World Rendering/high-precision camera-relative rendering with ED-Finder-scale coordinates; do not introduce an arbitrary application worldScale as truth. The runtime implements ED-Finder's semantic camera contract rather than exposing Babylon camera types. Include top-down and restrained pitched navigation, bounded/cancellable fly-to where appropriate, reduced-motion behavior, and exact meaningful camera/selection restoration in the isolated workbench. Implement the star path using instanced camera-facing quads/billboards or equivalent custom instance buffers. Do NOT use PointsCloudSystem/gl_PointSize and do NOT create one mesh per star. Normalize scene data into typed/compact buffers so React is not rebuilding GPU arrays per render. Use semantic/hysteretic LOD where needed and preserve guaranteed selected/highlighted/reference targets. Implement on-demand rendering so stable idle state stops continuous work; camera motion, transitions, hover/picking, streaming/dirty-layer changes may schedule frames. Keep this main-thread-first; do not add worker/offscreen complexity unless profiling proves it is required, because 27B explicitly defers that decision. Provide deterministic isolated workbench fixtures/controls at the accepted performance tiers: 20k and 40k production-like stars, 100k stress, 500k torture, and 1m extreme diagnostic. The 1m case is diagnostic, not a blanket device support promise. Report WebGPU and WebGL2 evidence separately where the environment permits. Centralize picking/target identity. The 27B workbench must compare/measure the accepted picking candidates — Babylon built-in instance picking, GPU ID-buffer picking, and CPU spatial index plus GPU confirmation — rather than silently declaring one winner without evidence. Preserve stable target identity between rendering, picking, selection and any labels. Collect non-personal telemetry appropriate to the accepted contract: backend, frame CPU/GPU duration where available, visible count, draw calls, resource count, buffer bytes, pick latency, and resource-loss/recovery outcome; no credentials or Commander History payloads. Add deterministic tests/fixtures for the renderer-neutral contracts and truth boundaries relevant to this workbench, including at minimum that ambient objects cannot become factual/selectable system targets and renderer-specific types do not escape. Reuse Stage 26 fixtures/tests only according to the Stage 27A inheritance matrix; do not blindly carry historical assumptions forward. Keep the workbench isolated behind a development-only entry/route or equivalent existing repo pattern. Production #map behavior, production bundle activation, deployment, and cutover are forbidden in 27B. Also OUT OF SCOPE: V3 implementation or ratings work, Journal ingestion/activation or Commander History product implementation, production data access/writes, database migrations, deployment, CRE mechanics changes, CPE mechanics/persistence changes, System Map implementation, colonised-system infrastructure, production feature parity/cutover, V2 archive work, or opportunistic cleanup unrelated to making the isolated workbench correct. Do not access production systems or credentials. Acceptance evidence must be concrete: focused unit/import-boundary tests, typecheck/lint/build as appropriate, isolated browser smoke/interaction checks at the repo's established required desktop viewports where practical, verification that the production map path is unchanged, deterministic fixture-tier evidence, backend/fallback/rebuild evidence that can be exercised in the available environment, telemetry/picking results with limitations stated rather than invented, and git diff --check. If hardware WebGPU/GPU timing or device-loss cannot be exercised on the worker hardware, implement the deterministic harness and record that limitation honestly; do not broaden scope or fake a pass. End with a concise summary of changed files, tests/measurements run, evidence, and remaining 27B risks. Do not begin Stage 27C or any later stage.
